BasisState.description:
Derivative premium over the reference price.

Always computed from venue mark prices, because last traded prices on thin
contracts produce a basis that reflects one stale trade rather than the market.

price_source.description: Which derivative price the basis was computed from.

BasisState.title: BasisState

CollectionTier.description:
How deeply an instrument or asset was collected in a generation.

Published on every state row so that a consumer never mistakes the absence of
a tier B metric for a zero (see ``docs/ARCHITECTURE.md``).
CollectionTier.title: CollectionTier

Coverage.description:
How much of the observable market a state row rests on.

Each family of metrics has its own coverage, because a state may have seven
price sources, five funding sources and three liquidity sources. One number
would hide that.

expected_venue_count.description: Venues that listed the asset and were expected to report this generation.
expected_venue_count.title: Expected Venue Count

listing_venue_count.description: Venues whose catalogue lists this asset at all.
listing_venue_count.title: Listing Venue Count

Coverage.title: Coverage

CrowdingComponents.description:
A vector of observable positioning-crowding components.

As with pressure, these are components rather than a ``Crowding: HIGH`` label.
CrowdingComponents.title: CrowdingComponents

DataQuality.description: The complete quality record attached to a state row.
DataQuality.title: DataQuality

DepthBand.description: Visible resting liquidity within one distance band of the reference price.
DepthBand.title: DepthBand

Dispersion.description:
How far venue prices sit from each other.

Uses robust statistics throughout, so that one malfunctioning venue widens the
measurement without destroying it.
Dispersion.title: Dispersion

FragmentationState.description: How fragmented an asset's market is across venues.

fragmentation_index.description: Composite of venue breadth, volume concentration and price dispersion.
fragmentation_index.title: Fragmentation Index

FragmentationState.title: FragmentationState

Freshness.description:
Per-family observation ages.

Published separately because a state's ticker data may be four minutes old
while its order books are fifty. Reporting one timestamp for all of it would be
a fabrication.
Freshness.title: Freshness

FundingState.description:
Perpetual funding across venues.

Native intervals are preserved and the 8-hour equivalent is a linear rescaling,
never a compounded one. Venues whose funding semantics Atlas cannot document are
excluded rather than assumed.

intervals_observed_hours.description: Distinct native funding intervals among contributing venues, sorted.
intervals_observed_hours.title: Intervals Observed Hours

FundingState.title: FundingState

GenomeState.description:
Market Genome lifecycle and, once available, its feature vector.

Features stay ``None`` until the minimum history exists. Atlas reports
``warming_up`` rather than emitting a fingerprint from insufficient data.

features.description: Normalised behavioural features. Empty unless status is available.
features.title: Features

GenomeState.title: GenomeState

GenomeStatus.description:
Market Genome lifecycle state.

Atlas will not emit genome features before the minimum history exists, and
says which state an asset is in rather than emitting approximate features.
GenomeStatus.title: GenomeStatus

ImpactEstimate.description:
The cost of consuming a given notional of visible liquidity.

Called an *observable order-book impact estimate* rather than slippage, because
it models only the visible book at one instant: no fees, no latency, no hidden
liquidity, no market response, no cancellation.

buy_depth_sufficient.description: Whether the sampled book held enough visible ask liquidity to fill.
buy_depth_sufficient.title: Buy Depth Sufficient

ImpactEstimate.title: ImpactEstimate

InstrumentType.description:
The kind of market an instrument represents.

Kept deliberately small. Venue-specific product names (OKX's ``SWAP``,
Kraken's ``flexible_futures``) are mapped onto these by their adapter, so that
no venue vocabulary reaches analytics.
InstrumentType.title: InstrumentType

LiquidationState.description:
Liquidation observations, kept venue-scoped by default.

Liquidation semantics differ so much between venues that an aggregate is only
published when the contributing venues' semantics are compatible. Otherwise the
per-venue observations stand alone.

note.description: Why an aggregate was or was not published.
note.title: Note

LiquidationState.title: LiquidationState

LiquidityState.description:
An asset's liquidity across venues.

The surface preserves venue contributions rather than only the aggregate, so a
consumer can see whether depth is one venue or ten.

book_imbalance_50bps.description: (bid depth - ask depth) / (bid depth + ask depth) at 50 bps. A structural measurement of the visible book, not a directional signal.
book_imbalance_50bps.title: Book Imbalance 50Bps

LiquidityState.title: LiquidityState

MarketStructure.description: Which market segments exist for an asset and on how many venues.

quote_currencies.description: Distinct quote asset IDs observed, sorted.
quote_currencies.title: Quote Currencies

MarketStructure.title: MarketStructure

ObservationOrigin.description:
How an observation entered the dataset.

A backfilled record is always distinguishable from one captured live, because
the two have different reliability and different timestamp semantics.
ObservationOrigin.title: ObservationOrigin

OpenInterestState.description:
Aggregate derivative open interest.

Only instruments whose open-interest unit is known, and whose contract
multiplier is published when the unit is contracts, are converted. The rest are
counted in ``excluded_instrument_count`` and their raw values remain available.

excluded_instrument_count.description: Instruments whose open interest could not be converted.
excluded_instrument_count.title: Excluded Instrument Count

OpenInterestState.title: OpenInterestState

PressureComponents.description:
A vector of observable market-pressure components.

Deliberately not collapsed into a score. Components absent for an asset are
``None``, and ``components_available`` says how many were computed, so that two
assets are only compared on the same basis.

baseline_window.description: Window the standardised components were measured against.
baseline_window.title: Baseline Window

derivative_flow_proxy.description: Reserved for aggressive derivative flow. Null in this release.
derivative_flow_proxy.title: Derivative Flow Proxy

spot_flow_proxy.description: Reserved for aggressive spot flow. Null in this release: Atlas does not collect a public trade tape, so there is no honest way to populate it.
spot_flow_proxy.title: Spot Flow Proxy

PressureComponents.title: PressureComponents

PriceSource.description:
Which venue-published price a value was taken from.

Recorded so that basis and dispersion are never computed from a mixture of
mark, mid and last prices without that being visible.
PriceSource.title: PriceSource

ReferencePrice.description:
The global reference price and how it was formed.

Named ``reference_price`` rather than ``price`` because no single true price
exists across a fragmented market, and because this value is not executable.

provenance_ref.description: Key into the evidence table. Provenance is referenced rather than inlined so a state row does not carry a large array (see docs/STORAGE.md).
provenance_ref.title: Provenance Ref

ReferencePrice.title: ReferencePrice

ReferencePriceMethod.description: How a global reference price was produced.
ReferencePriceMethod.title: ReferencePriceMethod

ResolutionState.description:
Confidence in an asset identity.

Only :attr:`RESOLVED` and :attr:`MANUAL_OVERRIDE` identities are aggregated
across venues. The others exist so that an uncertain identity can be recorded
without being merged (see ``docs/ASSET_RESOLUTION.md``).
ResolutionState.title: ResolutionState

ReturnsState.description: Fractional change in the reference price over several windows.
ReturnsState.title: ReturnsState

TechnicalState.description:
Technical indicators over the reference-price series.

Deliberately a small part of Atlas. These are measurements of the input series,
not recommendations, and Atlas does not emit buy or sell labels.

note.default: Computed on Atlas snapshot-cadence reference prices, so values are not comparable to indicators computed on a venue's own candles.
note.title: Note

TechnicalState.title: TechnicalState

VenueLiquidity.description: One venue's contribution to an asset's liquidity surface.

depth_share.description: This venue's share of 50 bps depth.
depth_share.title: Depth Share

VenueLiquidity.title: VenueLiquidity

VolatilityState.description: Realised volatility over several windows, with window coverage attached.

annualisation.description: How volatility was annualised. Stated so it is never ambiguous.
annualisation.title: Annualisation

sampling_interval_minutes.description: The snapshot cadence the series was sampled at.
sampling_interval_minutes.title: Sampling Interval Minutes

VolatilityState.title: VolatilityState

VolumeState.description:
Venue-reported trading volume, segmented by market type.

Every field is described as *reported*: Atlas relays what venues publish and
does not independently verify it.

venues_reporting_quote_volume.description: Venues that published quote-currency volume directly. Venues publishing only base volume are excluded from the USD totals rather than converted with a price they did not quote against.
venues_reporting_quote_volume.title: Venues Reporting Quote Volume

VolumeState.title: VolumeState

WindowCoverage.description:
How complete a rolling window's inputs are.

A 30-day percentile computed from two days of data is not a 30-day percentile.
Atlas publishes this so that a consumer can tell the difference, and returns
null for the metric itself when the window is too sparse.
WindowCoverage.title: WindowCoverage

description:
One asset's observable global market state at one snapshot time.

The object Atlas exists to produce. Sections are nested models; a section whose
inputs were unavailable is present with null fields rather than absent, so that
a consumer never has to guess whether a key is missing or the data was.

observed_at.description: Snapshot effective time in epoch milliseconds.
observed_at.title: Observed At

default.note: Computed on Atlas snapshot-cadence reference prices, so values are not comparable to indicators computed on a venue's own candles.

title: MarketState
